claims.text: HEA multilayers initially have mixed or partially coherent interfaces.
HEA multilayers without the engineered B2 interlayer predominantly deform by diffusion-mediated creep at high temperature.
Controlled Al addition can form a thin, ordered B2 interlayer between adjacent HEA layers.
The B2 interlayer can be made coherent with the surrounding HEA layers.
The lattice parameters of the B2 interlayer can be tuned to match those of the surrounding HEA layers.
Introducing the lattice-matched B2 interlayer improves interface coherency.
Both diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated deformation mechanisms are active under the proposed creep-test stresses and temperatures.
Enhanced coherency from the ordered B2 interlayer impedes atomic diffusion.
The coherent B2 interlayer facilitates dislocation nucleation.
The coherent B2 interlayer facilitates dislocation glide.
The combined suppression of diffusion and facilitation of dislocation motion shifts creep from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated behavior.
B2-containing HEA multilayers will exhibit reduced signatures of diffusion-mediated creep relative to controls without the interlayer.
B2-containing HEA multilayers will exhibit increased dislocation activity relative to controls without the interlayer.
B2-containing HEA multilayers will have modified creep-rate curves relative to controls without the interlayer.
The proposed transition depends on maintaining an optimal B2-interlayer thickness, composition, and lattice match.
Significant deviations from the optimal interlayer parameters may cause unwanted phase formation.
Significant deviations from the optimal interlayer parameters may degrade the HEA system's overall properties.
